summary: Olivia Chow's Instagram record on parks and environment centers on defending Ontario Place as public space, expanding access to park amenities, and advancing climate action. Chow opposes the provincial plan to build a private luxury spa at Ontario Place and the destruction of the West Island's 800 mature trees, and pledges to refuse to yield Toronto-owned land there. Chow opposes relocating the Ontario Science Centre. Chow supports keeping the waterfront publicly accessible, opening wading pools earlier in the summer, and city solutions like ReusableTO containers, sustainable packaging, and supports for small businesses going green. Chow frames a vision linking transit, safe streets, green space, clean rivers, climate-ready communities, and green jobs, and notes single-use plastics dominate park litter. A 2014 record references a McGregor Park revitalization completed in a single day.
